articles.title: Blackmagic’s Vision Pro immersive camera can be yours for only $29,995
articles.summary: The URSA Cine Immersive camera is up for preorder from Blackmagic, which will release it and a DaVinci Resolve update for Apple Vision Pro video support early next year.
articles.body: Blackmagic has announced that its URSA Cine Immersive commercial camera for shooting high-quality 3D immersive video is now available to preorder “direct from Blackmagic Design Offices,” with the first deliveries going out in early 2025. The camera, which could enable more immersive content for the Vision Pro, costs $29,995 — or a mere 8.6 Vision Pros. First revealed in June, the Cine Immersive will let cinematographers shoot 90fps video in stereoscopic 3D at 8160 x 7200 resolution per eye — or more than twice the estimated per-eye resolution of the Vision Pro’s screens. They’ll be able to edit the footage using the proprietary Apple Immersive Video format in DaVinci Resolve Studio, which Blackmagic plans to add support for early next year. Blackmagic Design CEO Grant Petty said the DaVinci update will enable “a true end-to-end workflow for Apple Immersive Video.” He added that the company is “looking forward to working closely with filmmakers” on immersive videos ahead of the camera’s wider release later in 2025. Blackmagic included images of the camera in its email to The Verge. It looks cool, so I’ve included them for your perusal: [Image: [Image: [Image: The Vision Pro has some immersive content outside of Apple’s videos — in apps like Amplium or Explore POV — but none of them quite have the quality of Apple’s videos. Until now, Apple has been the only company producing content with its format, and only a handful of such videos are available at this point. That could change, eventually, if studios take advantage of Blackmagic’s new camera and DaVinci update.

articles.title: Sharmila Tagore converted to Islam as she married Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi because it was necessary in those days, reveals Saba Pataudi: 'My grandmother wouldn't have allowed it any other way'
articles.summary: Veteran actor Sharmila Tagore converted to Islam and adopted the name Ayesha when she married legendary cricketer and former Indian cricket captain
articles.body: Veteran actor Sharmila Tagore converted to Islam and adopted the name Ayesha when she married legendary cricketer and former Indian cricket captain Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi, fondly known as Tiger Pataudi. The couple's marriage attracted considerable attention at the time, with Sharmila's conversion becoming a subject of controversy. The two also reportedly received death threats following their wedding.Years later, the couple's younger daughter, jewellery designer and tarot reader Saba Ali Khan Pataudi, has opened up about her mother's decision to convert. During a conversation with Siddharth Kannan, Saba explained that the conversion was necessary for the marriage to be formally recognised under the customs and traditions followed by Mansoor's family. She also suggested that her paternal grandmother would not have approved of the marriage otherwise.“In those days, conversion was necessary. The children are legitimate because of conversion, which legalised things. It was a necessity and not something one could consider if or not to do,” she shared. When asked why conversion was necessary, Saba explained that it was a requirement from the perspective of the prevailing system and traditions.She further pointed out that certain religious customs and requirements applied when a Muslim man married someone from another faith. According to Saba, the marriage would not have been accepted or acknowledged within the family if Sharmila had not converted. “My grandmother (Mansoor’s mother) would surely not have allowed it in any other way,” she stated.Saba also clarified that her mother's conversion did not come in the way of her acting career or professional identity. She said Mansoor was “liberated in his thoughts” and never imposed restrictions on Sharmila after their marriage. According to her, neither Mansoor nor his family insisted that the actor change her name on her passport or other official documents, which could have affected her professional life.“It didn’t take away from her personality or her profession,” Saba added.Speaking about the family's religious beliefs and upbringing, Saba revealed that religion was never imposed on the children. While she personally follows Islam, like her father, she said the family celebrated festivals belonging to different faiths, including Holi, Diwali and Eid.She emphasised that both her parents allowed their children the freedom to follow their individual beliefs and practices. “We were always allowed to follow our own path by both our parents,” Saba noted.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: We read Sofia Franklyn’s memoir about her falling-out with Alex Cooper so you don’t have to
articles.summary: “Daddy Issues” is a tell-all from Franklyn’s side about the end of her business relationship and friendship with Cooper, who went on to helm “Call Her Daddy”...
articles.body:
The "Daddy Gang" is finally getting to hear from the co-"founding father" of "Call Her Daddy."

Sofia Franklyn, who co-created the famous podcast with Alex Cooper, on Tuesday released her memoir, "Daddy Issues," in which she details her falling-out with her now ex-friend.

The duo shot to viral fame in 2018, when the podcast was still under Barstool Sports. It became known for candid conversations about commonly taboo topics for women to discuss publicly, including raunchy sex stories.

But the two professionally split up in 2020, news that initially shocked their listeners. Cooper went on to host the podcast solo, eventually moving it to Spotify and now SiriusXM in lucrative deals that helped propel her to mainstream success.

Meanwhile, Franklyn, who is an influencer with over 619,000 Instagram followers, launched her own podcast titled "Sofia with an F."

Over the years, rumors had circulated about what exactly happened between Franklyn and Cooper. Here are some of the biggest claims in Franklyn's 240-page book.

Franklyn writes about struggling to find a clear path as she was growing up in Utah with a single mom. She was arrested three times: once for using a fake ID and twice for underage drinking. Eventually, she left to start anew in New York City, largely to escape an abusive relationship.

But her early days in the city were far from ideal. She lived with her aunt and was working at Morgan Stanley in a job under a toxic boss who she claims harassed her regularly. She eventually moved into her own place, which she could barely afford, and found herself feeling extremely lonely.

A random girl Franklyn befriended in a ride-share connected her to Cooper and her childhood friend Lauren, who were looking for a third roommate.

Cooper and Franklyn ended up becoming inseparable, with Lauren largely out of the picture as she spent much of her time with her boyfriend. But one night, Franklyn writes, she and Lauren shared a rare evening in the apartment alone together.

That's when Lauren asked Franklyn whether she thought it was weird that Cooper had "tossed" her aside.

"You showed up and it was like I never existed," Franklyn said Lauren told her, which prompted Franklyn to apologize.

Lauren also told Franklyn that Cooper "uses you because you're hot, to like, go to parties and stuff."

At the time, Franklyn wrote, she felt defensive of her friendship with Cooper and did not think of Cooper as "using" her.

But later, another close friend of Cooper's from childhood also seemed to warn her that Cooper was not going to stick with her.

Muji, known to early "Call Her Daddy" listeners as "Milfhunter," worked on the podcast with the duo. He told Franklyn that Cooper "doesn't have friends. I've watched it happen since high school."

When Cooper abruptly fired Muji, Franklyn said, he told her: "She's gonna f--- you."

An alleged firing attempt, secret raise and IP disagreement

Cooper and Franklyn's stars rose quickly at Barstool as the two took creative control of their show with company founder Dave Portnoy's blessing.

But Franklyn started to feel things change after the Barstool holiday party. That night, she felt "insane anxiety," drank excessively and fought with Cooper.

An angry Cooper told Franklyn she was "rude" and "aggressive" toward her at the party and that everyone, including Portnoy, had noticed and wanted to fire her.

Franklyn says she wanted to apologize to Portnoy for her behavior but was told not to by Cooper. When she finally did say something, Portnoy appeared to dismiss it, saying that "the girls got in a fight."

It wasn't until later, Franklyn writes, that she learned Cooper had used the party as a way to negotiate a raise for herself.

Muji purportedly told her that Cooper said, "If I have to put up with her, I need more money." She got the raise: $20,000 more than Franklyn every year.

"She didn't tell you because she didn't want you to know she tried to get you fired," Franklyn said Muji told her.

Franklyn writes that in 2020, when the duo were negotiating their new contract together, they sent Barstool an email with a new proposal asking for a "50/50 split of all revenue derived from Barstool's exploitation of the property (i.e., advertisers, sponsors, merch, etc.)" and a "minimum guarantee — $1M each, per year."

The negotiations centered on the intellectual property for "Call Her Daddy," which Barstool Sports owned and could technically continue without Franklyn or Cooper attached.

Amid their talks with Barstool, Franklyn said, she and Cooper agreed their goal was to stay together. They even came up with a spinoff podcast in case the negotiations fell through, titling it "The Fathers."

"We're being corny as s---, but it's because we're both blissed out on the plan and our future — we don't know how Barstool will respond, but we know that staying together is more important than losing the IP, or whatever they may threaten. What is the name without us?"

But in the end, Franklyn was ousted as co-host. Portnoy called Franklyn to tell her that Cooper had met with him separately and proposed going on without her.

"She came to me with a plan, and I needed an episode. There's no clear favorite," he told her, according to Franklyn's memoir. "You could always have your own show, and we promote the s--- out of it like we did with Call Her Daddy . I think it would be huge."

Portnoy also said Cooper had hired her own lawyer and claimed that Franklyn had been "the one that's been dragging this on, and she's been ready to sign this thing."

Franklyn claims Cooper subsequently locked her out of their shared social accounts and posted a 52-minute YouTube breakup video called " The Truth about Call Her Daddy " in which she described Franklyn as a "liability." Six years later, the video is still up, and it has amassed 4.6 million views.

Representatives for Portnoy and Cooper did not respond to requests for comment Tuesday.

The book opens with a scene in which Franklyn's book agent calls her to say she had received an angry call from Matt Kaplan.

Kaplan, a Hollywood producer, married Cooper in 2024. The couple co-founded the Unwell Network, a subsidiary of the media company Trending.

Franklyn writes that her agent told her Kaplan said Cooper would sue.

Representatives from Unwell told The New York Times that Kaplan "never discussed the book's claims or any intent to sue the author with Verve."

A representative for Kaplan did not respond to a request for comment Tuesday.

articles.title: Dani García, chef: “La ensalada césar más rica no se hace con lechuga, sino con tomate azul, dos yemas de huevo, dos anchoas y 30 gramos de queso parmesano rallado”
articles.standfirst: El cocinero marbellí reinventa el clásico con el tomate como protagonista
articles.summary: El cocinero marbellí reinventa el clásico con el tomate como protagonista
articles.body: La ensalada césar es uno de esos platos que casi nadie se atreve a tocar. Lechuga romana, picatostes, parmesano y su inconfundible salsa forman una combinación que se repite en restaurantes de medio mundo. Dani García, sin embargo, ha decidido darle la vuelta. El chef andaluz ha compartido en sus redes una versión en la que la lechuga desaparece y el tomate pasa a ocupar el centro del plato. Tras años preparándola de la forma clásica, el cocinero se plantea una pregunta sencilla: “¿Por qué no hacerla con un gran tomate?”. Para su receta elige el tomate azul, una variedad que llama la atención por el tono violeta oscuro, casi negro, de su piel. Si no se encuentra, propone alternativas como el rosa de Barbastro o el raf. Lo importante es que esté maduro pero firme, ya que se corta en láminas muy finas y un tomate blando terminaría deshecho. El secreto está, como en la receta original, en el aliño. Para dos tomates hacen falta dos yemas de huevo, 30 mililitros de aceite de oliva virgen extra, unas gotas de zumo de limón, una cucharadita de mostaza, dos filetes de anchoa en salazón y 30 gramos de parmesano rallado. El primer paso es triturar las anchoas hasta convertirlas en una especie de puré. Después se añaden las yemas y la mostaza y se va incorporando el aceite poco a poco para montar una emulsión, que se termina con el limón y el queso. Solo queda cortar los tomates y cubrirlos con la salsa. Quien prefiera no usar huevo crudo puede recurrir a yemas pasteurizadas, que se venden en muchos supermercados y funcionan igual. El resultado conserva la esencia de la César, con el punto salino de la anchoa y la cremosidad del huevo, pero con la frescura del tomate. Una versión que, curiosamente, se aleja del original creado en 1924 en Tijuana por el italiano Caesar Cardini, que tampoco llevaba anchoas.

articles.title: I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! 2026 - see the line-up in full
articles.summary: The football star will be joined by Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page and YouTuber Sharky among others.
articles.body:
Former England and Manchester United footballer Wayne Rooney, Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page and YouTuber Sharky will be among the intrepid crew entering the jungle Down Under for this year's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here!

They will be joined by Kaiser Chiefs frontman Ricky Wilson, Paralympian and presenter Ade Adepitan, actress Claire Sweeney and broadcaster Mariella Frostrup.

TV presenter AJ Odudu, comedian Jack Skipper, Love Island contestant Chloe Burrows and model Leomie Anderson round out the team headed for Australia.

Hosts Ant and Dec will return with the ITV show's opening episode on Monday, 16 November, with the series now in its 26th year.

Ade Adepitan - Paralympian and documentary maker, who will be the first wheelchair user in the show's history

Leomie Anderson - Model and co-host of Glow Up: Britain's Next Make-Up Star

Chloe Burrows - Love Island finalist, Kiss Radio breakfast presenter and host of Chloe vs The World podcast

Mariella Frostrup - Broadcaster, author and journalist, including appearances on Loose Women and Times Radio

AJ Odudu - Big Brother presenter and former Strictly Come Dancing contestant

Joanna Page - Stacey from hit sitcom Gavin and Stacey, and host of TV series including Shift the Thrift and Shop Well For Less

Wayne Rooney - Former Everton, Manchester United and England striker turned football manager and pundit

Sharky - one of YouTube's Beta Squad (alongside Celebrity Traitors star King Kenny among others), who have 12 million subscribers

Jack Skipper - Stand-up comedian and social media star

Claire Sweeney - Coronation Street and Brookside star and musical actress

Ricky Wilson - Kaiser Chiefs singer, ex-Virgin Radio drivetime host and former The Voice UK coach

Rooney is following in the footsteps of his wife Coleen, who was runner-up on I'm A Celebrity in 2024.

"If you're going in you want to win it," he said. "Coleen's already tried and obviously she finished second in the show so I'm here to bring that title back to the Rooney household."

Rooney admitted that jumping out of a helicopter is his biggest fear. "I've been booked to jump out of a plane three times before and never made it on the plane," he said.

"I don't like snakes or what is in the water either - I don't go in the sea."

Producers are making adaptations to the Australian jungle camp so it is accessible for Adepitan.

In a press statement, he said: "For me, this is a moment in time. Even if I go out in the first week, I will always be remembered as the person in a wheelchair. I am slightly overwhelmed. It's never been done before, and it never crossed my mind I would be the first."

Keith Lemon comedian Leigh Francis is not among the official line-up but is rumoured to become a late addition.

The last I'm A Celebrity series was the all-star version in South Africa, which was marked by heated arguments and walk-outs among the cast during the live final in April.

articles.title: Katy Perry's comment that ex 'should be in jail' resurfaces after Russell Brand's prison sentencing
articles.summary: From Kate Moss to Katy Perry to wife Laura Gallacher Brand, Russell Brand's romantic history spans high-profile romances and a headline-making divorce.
articles.body: Russell Brand's romantic past is drawing renewed attention following his prison sentencing, including ex-wife Katy Perry's description of his behavior during their marriage as "very controlling." Years before the comedian was convicted of rape and sexual assault, Perry said Brand struggled with her role as "the boss" of her own career and shared how their whirlwind marriage ended with a text message in which he announced he wanted a divorce. Now, her past comments are resurfacing alongside renewed interest in Brand’s relationship history, from his brief romance with Spice Girls singer Geri Halliwell to his marriage to his current wife Laura Brand, who testified in his defense. RUSSELL BRAND SENTENCED AFTER RAPE, SEXUAL ASSAULT CONVICTIONS IN UK Here's a look back at Brand's most notable relationships. Kate Moss — 2006 Brand described a brief romantic encounter with Kate Moss in his memoir, "Booky Wook 2: This Time It's Personal," writing that their connection elevated his celebrity status. "I could never have anticipated the instant elevation that this liaison would afford me, it was like being awarded a celebrity Victoria Cross," he wrote, according to the New York Post. The comedian, who met Moss through a mutual friend, expressed his admiration for the model in the book. "Kate Moss is the prettiest girl in all our schools," he wrote. "Behold our queen, but don’t look at her directly or all else you gaze upon till death brings down your lids will be as shadows compared to her beauty." In the book, Brand wrote that he became smitten, but their connection faded after he publicly downplayed the encounter to journalists. Teresa Palmer — 2008 Brand and Australian actress Teresa Palmer briefly dated after meeting while filming "Bedtime Stories" in 2008. By July of that year, both were publicly discussing their relationship, with Brand suggesting he was ready to leave his womanizing reputation behind. "I’m a changed man," he said at the time, according to Cosmopolitan. "I’ve met someone very beautiful and I’ve settled down." Palmer expressed similar enthusiasm about their budding romance. "We’ve only been together for a month, but it’s going brilliantly," she said, according to the outlet. The pair attended the O2 Silver Clef Awards together in London on July 4, 2008, but their relationship was short-lived. By the fall of 2008, the couple had separated. KATY PERRY SNUBS FAMOUS EXES BEFORE SWEET NOD TO JUSTIN TRUDEAU IN CHEEKY ONSTAGE MOMENT Katy Perry — 2009–2012 Brand and Katy Perry, who met on the set of "Get Him to the Greek" in 2009, announced their engagement in January 2010 before marrying in India on Oct. 23 of that year. Their marriage lasted approximately 14 months before Brand filed for divorce in December 2011. Perry later discussed their relationship in a 2013 Vogue interview, describing behavior she considered "controlling." So that was really hurtful, and it was very controlling, which was upsetting," she said. "I felt a lot of responsibility for it ending, but then I found out the real truth, which I can’t necessarily disclose because I keep it locked in my safe for a rainy day. I let go, and I was like: This isn’t because of me, this is beyond me. So I have moved on from that." During the interview, Perry said Brand informed her of his divorce plans by text message. The moment she received the message was captured on camera and featured in the pop star's 2012 documentary "Katy Perry: Part of Me." Following Brand's sentencing, another video showing an interaction between Brand and Perry gained traction online. During an interview at the 2010 Vanity Fair Oscar party, Brand appeared to criticize Perry for swearing on camera and displayed a badge bearing the word "Obey." "He didn’t like her getting more attention than him," one social media user wrote on X. Months before his conviction, Perry made a pointed remark about an ex during a concert in July at Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire, England. While playing an interactive game that asked audience members to act out their reaction to seeing an ex, Perry said, "I hope my ex isn’t here. He should be in jail," according to The Mirror. Perry did not specifically name Brand. Isabella Brewster — Summer 2012 Brand began dating Isabella Brewster, a former talent agent, following his split from Perry. The pair reportedly met at a yoga class. He confirmed their romance during a July 18, 2012, appearance on Howard Stern's radio show, just days after his divorce became final. "Some things in the newspaper aren’t true … that’s true, actually," Brand said when asked about Brewster, according to E! News. According to Cosmopolitan, the pair were reportedly considering renting a home together in Los Angeles. By late August, however, the romance had ended. "Isabella and [Russell] broke it off," a source told Us Weekly at the time. "He has been in London since the Olympics and is traveling for standup." Geri Halliwell — August 2012 Following his split from Brewster, Brand was briefly linked to Spice Girls singer Geri Halliwell. The pair reportedly grew close during preparations for the 2012 London Olympics' closing ceremony, at which both performed. They were photographed holding hands during a visit to Hampton Court Palace with Halliwell’s daughter, Bluebell, and were also reportedly spotted enjoying a picnic on Hampstead Heath. "He isn’t ready to settle down so soon after coming out of marriage," a source told The Mirror. Jemima Goldsmith — 2013–2014 Brand began dating producer and journalist Jemima Goldsmith in 2013. Their relationship lasted approximately a year, during which the comedian publicly expressed his love for her and said their connection felt different from his previous romances. "I really love her. I’m very, very happy in a relationship that feels very different from anything I’ve experienced before," Brand reportedly said during a 2014 appearance on "The Jonathan Ross Show." Their breakup was reported in September 2014. In a statement posted on X following his sentencing, she accused him of "violence, coercive control and abuse." She alleged that she had called police to have him removed from her home during a violent incident in 2014. Goldsmith said she chose not to pursue charges or speak publicly at the time because she feared the impact of media attention on her teenage children. "I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014," she wrote. Laura Gallacher Brand — 2006–2007; reunited in 2015, married in 2017 Brand’s relationship with his current wife, Laura Gallacher Brand, began years before his marriage to Perry. Gallacher, an author and illustrator whose sister is British broadcaster Kirsty Gallacher, first became involved with Brand in 2006. She was 19 and he was 31. Their initial relationship ended the following year amid his reported difficulty with monogamy. "When I met him, I was aware that he liked women, and I was aware toward the latter half of that year that he was engaging with other women," Laura told the court during Brand's trial, according to Sky News. "I was not interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people. I was invested; we both had told each other we loved each other, but it was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous." After Brand’s marriage to Perry ended, he and Laura reconnected in 2015. The couple welcomed daughter Mabel in November 2016 before marrying on Aug. 26, 2017, in a ceremony near Henley-on-Thames, England. Their family later grew with the birth of their daughter Peggy in July 2018 and a son in 2023. Laura publicly defended her husband during his 2026 rape and sexual assault trial. articles.title: I'm a Celebrity: Gavin and Stacey's Joanna Page gets message from Nessa
articles.summary: Ruth Jones sends a message from 'Nessa' to co-star Joanna Page as Page prepares for her jungle debut.
articles.body:
Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page has confirmed she will appear on the upcoming reality TV series I'm a Celebrity, with her former co-star Ruth Jones urging her to "have a crackin' time".

Page, who played Stacey Shipman in the BBC comedy, is joining this year's line-up of celebrities on the forthcoming show in Australia.

The 49-year-old, from Swansea, said she had her sights on becoming the first Welsh Queen of the Jungle.

"You makes Barry very proud, I'm not gonna lie," said Jones - assuming her former Gavin & Stacey character Nessa Jenkins - on Instagram.

"They're gonna make you stick all manner of matter in your gob. And I'm not talking Gwen's omelettes... Just don't over do it, alrigh'? You knows what a weak constitution you has."

Speaking ahead of her trip down under, Page said she believed her co-stars will be "shocked" when she arrives in the jungle for the ITV reality show.

"I also know they will find it funny. They know exactly what I am like and they will laugh."

Page said being the first Welsh queen would be a "pretty good title to take home", but added she was just as excited to see how long she could last.

"I'm going to see this to the end and I'm going to be strong. I am going to get the most out of this."

As a mother-of-four, Page said she hoped her part in the show will help her "reconnect" with who she was before becoming a mum.

"This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. I'm very much an impulsive person and I just make a gut decision, so I said 'yes' straight away," said Page.

She said she hoped to find "peace and time for my thoughts" away from the everyday worries about feeding the children and getting everyone ready for the school run.

"I can be me, I can be Jo and not just mummy all the time. I think that will be nice."

"I will never get to do anything like this again. I am telling myself, 'Come on Jo, let's take yourself off to Australia and give yourself an experience'.

"It's exciting and it's going to be life-changing."

Page will enter the jungle alongside footballer Wayne Rooney, TV personality Chloe Burrows and soap star Claire Sweeney.

Rooney will follow in his wife Coleen's footsteps after she finished as runner-up on the 2024 series, and said he hoped "people will see me for who I am".

He said he had "always wanted to do" the show, joking that because of his short-lived football managerial career, he had more time on his hands.

"I like to have fun and I like to think I am actually a fun guy to be around.

"I do like to mess around a bit and I do talk a lot. People will have their own opinions, but I hope they will see me as a genuine person."

Page will be also joined by Paralympian and TV presenter Ade Adepitan - who will be the first contestant in a wheelchair to appear on the show – something he said his eight-year-old self would not believe.

"Words like 'honour' and 'privilege' are the ones I feel, but I don't think they sum it up enough," he said.

"For me, this is a moment in time. Even if I go out in the first week, I will always be remembered as the person in a wheelchair. I am slightly overwhelmed.

"It's never been done before, and it never crossed my mind I would be the first.

I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! starts on Monday, 16 November at 21:00 GMT on ITV.

articles.title: Un piquete entra en el plató de Gemma Nierga en RTVE y obliga a suspender ‘Cafè d’idees’: “No podemos hacer nuestro trabajo”
articles.standfirst: La periodista reivindica: "Los periodistas somos considerados servicios esenciales..."
articles.summary: La periodista reivindica: "Los periodistas somos considerados servicios esenciales..."
articles.body: Los medios de comunicación también han contado con incidencias distintas, pero una de las que más ha impactado ha sido la que ha sucedido en el espacio de TVE en Cataluña con el programa de Gemma Nierga y ha ocurrido en pleno directo. Un piquete ha entrado en el plató y provocado que el programa no pudiera seguir con su habitual transcurrir. Un grupo de manifestantes ha irrumpido en el plató de 'Cafè d'idees', el programa presentado en La 2 Cat, obligando a interrumpir la emisión en directo pese a contar con los servicios mínimos establecidos para la jornada. Ahora bien, Nierga ha denunciado públicamente que el piquete estaba impidiendo el trabajo de los periodistas. "Este programa había preparado un programa especial, pero no podemos hacer nuestro trabajo porque un grupo de manifestantes ha accedido al plató impidiendo que ejerzamos nuestro derecho a informar y que vosotros tengáis el derecho a recibir información", ha señalado en ese instante. Además, la periodista se ha lamentado porque considera el papel esencial de los medios de comunicación durante las jornadas de huelga. "Los periodistas somos considerados servicios esenciales, pero no podemos hacer nuestro trabajo". Esto provocaba la obligación a suspender temporalmente el programa de Nierga, cuya cuenta oficial ha confirmado que la emisión estaba siendo alterada por dichas movilizaciones en el plató concretamente. Alrededor de las 8:45 horas, después de unos 45 minutos de interrupción, 'Cafè d'idees' ha podido recuperar su programación en directo.

articles.title: Usher and Chris Brown Cancel Two More Performances as Feud Reports Heat Up
articles.summary: Amid reports of an ongoing feud, Usher and Chris Brown have canceled two more performances on their dual-headlining "R&B Tour," bringing the total number of...
articles.body:
Amid reports of an ongoing feud, Usher and Chris Brown have canceled two more performances on their dual-headlining "R&B Tour," bringing the total number of canceled concerts to six. The canceled dates were all added to the tour's original itinerary in August.

The latest cancellations are the November 16 performance at Los Angeles' SoFi Stadium and a December 6 show at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami. Both events are now listed as canceled on Ticketmaster, although nine more dates remain before the tour is scheduled to conclude in Tampa, Florida on Dec. 12.

The cancelations come amid widespread but unconfirmed reports of feuding between the two headliners, with rumors of a loud argument taking place backstage in Atlanta.

Reps for the two artists and Live Nation, the tour's promoter, did not immediately respond to Variety 's requests for comment.

The previous cancelations were in Baltimore, Cincinnati, South Carolina and Indianapolis. At the time, organizers cited a need to "prioritize the health and well-being of the touring party and crew," according to a statement from Indianapolis' Lucas Oil Stadium cited by Ticket News .

"The demands of a tour of this length and scale are significant, and these adjustments will allow the tour to continue safely and sustainably through the remaining scheduled performances," the statement continued.

Ordinarily, the canceled shows would be considered the result of an overreach — that the ticket demand had already largely been satisfied. However, they come in the wake of the controversial November 5 concert at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, which was marred by long delays, sound-quality issues and the pair not performing together, as they had on earlier dates of the tour. According to a report in TMZ , the dispute was over the concert's start time, with Brown arguing to delay the show for fans caught in heavy local traffic. The show was delayed for three hours, angering fans. TMZ states that the pair still have not resolved their differences; Brown has a long history of aggressive behavior, most notably his assault on Rihanna in 2009 .

Despite the drama, the tour has apparently been a major success: According to Pollstar, it grossed more than $280 million through October 3.

articles.title: Sidharth Malhotra was unbothered about Kiara Advani's intimate scenes with Yash in 'Toxic', says the actress as she breaks silence on the controversy and trolling: 'Been happening...from Aishwarya to many actresses'
articles.summary: Kiara Advani has finally breaks silence on the backlash she faced over her intimate scenes with Yash in ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’, admitting
articles.body: Kiara Advani has finally breaks silence on the backlash she faced over her intimate scenes with Yash in ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’, admitting that the film's initial response left her emotionally disappointed. The actor discussed the experience during her appearance on ‘Koffee With Karan Season 9’, where she was accompanied by her husband, Sidharth Malhotra. The episode also saw the couple speak about their personal life, including the news of their second pregnancy, which they announced in early October 2026.Speaking to host Karan Johar about the film's box-office performance and audience response, Kiara admitted that she found it difficult to deal with the reaction during the opening weekend. Despite the film getting off to a strong start, its reception did not match the team's expectations. Recalling how she felt, she said, “On day one, it is heartbreaking. Especially for this film, because as a team in totality any of us saw this coming. When it misfired despite it opening to what it did. It was heartbreaking for me that first weekend. I was very low about it,”However, the actor also spoke about the positive feedback she received for stepping outside her comfort zone and taking up a role that was different from her previous performances. She added, “But, then, there was a lot of appreciation. The fact that I had gone outside of my comfort zone playing that role. I think in my journey this will be defining.”The conversation also touched upon the controversy surrounding the song ‘Tabaahi’, following which Kiara faced considerable trolling over her intimate scenes with Yash. Several social media users questioned her decision to perform such scenes, bringing her marriage and motherhood into the discussion. Sidharth Malhotra was also dragged into the controversy, with many speculating about how he would have reacted to watching his wife in intimate scenes with another actor.Karan Johar pointed out the gender bias behind such reactions, highlighting how married male actors are seldom subjected to similar scrutiny for performing intimate scenes on screen. Responding to the discussion, Kiara made it clear that Sidharth was never bothered by the controversy and had not even brought up the subject with her. She said, “He had not cared about it. He has never brought it up. We have never spoken about it. It did not affect him, he was not bothered,”The actor also observed that women in the film industry have been subjected to such judgement for years, pointing out that several actresses before her have faced similar scrutiny. Referring to the larger pattern, she said, “It has been happening now for donkey years, for decades. From Aishwarya to so many wonderful actors,”Interestingly, Kiara revealed that she did not feel compelled to justify her choices or respond to the criticism. She was also encouraged by the number of people who called out the hypocrisy surrounding the backlash. Explaining her approach, she said, "What I must touch upon is when I was seeing what was going on the internet, there was a massive reaction of people who had already started calling it out, the hypocrisy, and I really did not feel the need to even justify,"Directed by Geetu Mohandas, ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ marked Yash's first film after the success of ‘KGF: Chapter 2’. Set in post-independence Goa, the gangster drama explores a world of crime, violence, power struggles and shifting loyalties. Yash plays two characters, Raya and his son Rumi, while Kiara portrays Nadia, Rumi's mother.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Brandon Sklenar got 'massive' to play a Delta Force operator in Taylor Sheridan's 'F.A.S.T.'
articles.summary: Brandon Sklenar reveals he got "massive" to play a Delta Force operator in Taylor Sheridan's "F.A.S.T.," a DEA black op thriller for Warners.
articles.body: Brandon Sklenar is shining a light on his transformation for the upcoming movie "F.A.S.T." The film is being made by "Yellowstone" creator Taylor Sheridan, and while not a lot of details are known, the publicly released plot is pretty epic. It's stated as follows: JOSH BROLIN CONFIRMS SICARIO 3 'IS HAPPENING' AS TAYLOR SHERIDAN FRANCHISE PREPARES TO RETURN F.A.S.T. concerns a former special forces commando, down on his luck after he returns Stateside, who is tapped by the DEA to lead a black op strike team against CIA-protected drug dealers in his town. TAYLOR SHERIDAN HAS WRITTEN THE SCRIPT FOR 'SICARIO 3' AS FRANCHISE GEARS UP FOR RETURN Sounds like it's right up the alley of anyone who loved "Sicario," and Sklenar will lead the way. Brandon Sklenar talks transformation for upcoming Taylor Sheridan movie. Sklenar spoke with "The Hollywood Reporter" about the upcoming movie, which is scheduled to premiere in May 2027, and revealed he had to bulk up for the role. "I put on a bunch of size for another film I had done earlier in the year. I’m starring in this film Taylor Sheridan wrote called F.A.S.T. for Warners. It’s coming out in May. I played a Delta Force operator, and I got massive," the former "1923" star told the outlet. What's interesting about Sklenar's comments is one very simple fact: Most Tier One operators (the U.S. military has five Tier One units), do not look anything like bodybuilders. In fact, I know several former operators who are fairly short and wiry. Being a massive person with a bodybuilder physique isn't overly advantageous when you need to ruck through mountains or blend in during low visibility operations. SEAL TEAM 6 MEMBER EXPLAINS BLUNT REALITY OF COMBAT AND EXPECTATIONS IN THE BLACK OPS WORLD Hollywood, for reasons that will never make sense to me, decides to portray commandos as if they're all physical super humans. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER There are Delta Force commandos who look like your local accountant or the science teacher at your nearby high school. There were multiple members of the operation to kill Osama bin Laden who didn't come close to cracking 6'0", including the mysterious point man going up to the third deck. articles.title: Once upon a time, crackers purified air, didn’t pollute: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
articles.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat says earlier firecrackers purified air and killed insects, urges “pure” festival celebrations, and notes Diwali’s global rise.
articles.body: NAGPUR: Firecrackers in earlier times were not made from chemicals, and their smoke killed insects and purified the atmosphere, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat said, adding that there is a scientific reason behind it. “Festivals keep the society ‘alive’ and will never stop despite some people trying to do so,” he said.Bhagwat pointed out that a “special kind” of air prevailed in the environment as ghee lamps and oil lamps were lit. “Such practices should be followed with an understanding of the science behind them. This will keep the atmosphere pure, and also bring joy to our life,” he said.The RSS chief was speaking at a Diwali event of Maheshwari Panchayat in Nagpur on Tuesday. Stressing that festivals are part of the fabric of Indian society, he said, “Festivals have been held since eternal times and they will continue.”On how festivals should be celebrated, Bhagwat said, “They should continue in their pure form, so that we keep getting the benefits they are meant to give. If all of us take care of this, we won’t have to worry about anything in life. Because of this, a person, society and humanity across the world remain safe along with the environment.”Bhagwat said Diwali is now getting its due place of importance across the world. “Diwali was earlier celebrated only in India, but is now celebrated in the parliaments of US and UK too. The world is realising that Indians should be wished on Diwali, knowing this is a day when every Indian is joyful, clean, pure and ready to serve, because doing charity at festivals is also our tradition,” he said.The RSS chief also asked people to follow rules that govern society. “In the house, society and city where we live, rules and laws are for all and framed to make everyone’s life good. articles.title: Kelsey Grammer still feels 'sense of smallness' for not serving in military: 'I do my best to make up for it'
articles.summary: Kelsey Grammer's giant screen film, "America the Beautiful," celebrates national parks and military sacrifice ahead of its Veterans Day premiere.
articles.body: Kelsey Grammer feels he missed an opportunity to give back to his country by not serving in the military when he was younger. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 71-year-old actor discussed his latest project, "America the Beautiful," a 40-minute giant screen documentary, and why he always does his best to "show up for the military" when he is able to. "I will always have an annoying sort of sense of smallness that I didn't serve, but I do my best to make up for it," he said. He explained that, despite feeling that way, he is unsure if he would have made a different decision if given the opportunity to do his life over again, noting, "It was a really interesting time." HOLLYWOOD MARINE VETERAN ROB RIGGLE DOUBTS MODERN STARS WOULD MAKE JIMMY STEWART'S WWII SACRIFICE WATCH: Kelsey Grammer feels a ‘sense of smallness’ for not having served in the military When he was a young man, he said, the Vietnam War was "sort of in full flair," and he had signed up for the draft and was ready to go fight had his number been drawn, but "President Nixon pulled us out just before I would have gone down to get my number." "So, I was thankful for not having to go, make that decision, but I would've gone. If my number had been up, I woulda gone. But I was, I was thankful not to," he said. "I used to work in San Diego. It was one of my first jobs at the Shakespeare Festival there, and I would go over to the Point Loma Military Graveyard and have a lunch sometimes. And I'd sit next to this cross that I'd found of a young man who was really only eight months older than I was who had died in Vietnam. And it just broke my heart." As a father, Grammer says he speaks to his children about the many sacrifices people have made to ensure the safety of America, adding he "will always try and instruct them with the idea that service to your country is a good idea." KELSEY GRAMMER WARNS OF CHILLING DANGER FACING AMERICANS WHO FORGET NATION'S FOUNDING HISTORY WATCH: Kelsey Grammer’s grandfather was an ‘inspiration’ to him He says that together they discuss the Revolutionary War and all the great battles throughout history, noting he would encourage them to serve their country if they wanted to, but "their mom would get mad at me." He noted, however, that this is something "people have been doing" for many years. "There's a lot of wonderful patriotic people in our country today whose children and whose husbands and wives are serving, and my hat is off to them all. And we salute them. I mean, with this particular thing, the 11 hour, the 11 day, 11th month, Armistice Day originally, now Veterans Day at the end of the first World War. Remarkable. The number of people who died in that war," he said. "So, certainly the hope was that it would never happen again and, sure enough, a generation later, we were fighting World War II. Amazing. And we go on. We continue. Hopefully it'll end one day." Grammer feels a strong connection to Veterans Day since his grandfather served as a colonel in the Army Corps of Engineers during World War II. When speaking about his grandfather, the "Frasier" star said he "was always an inspiration to me." "I looked up to him like a kid would," he said. "I mean, he raised me, but his bravery and his courage and his commitment to the country, these were active, living, breathing things that he was … he embodied that. And, so, it's always been my hope to kind of pass that along a little bit. At least a remembrance of him, respect for what he was able to do in the face of extraordinary hardship." CARRIE UNDERWOOD, GARY SINISE LEAD STARS WHO'VE SHARED WHY THEY'RE PROUD TO BE AMERICANS One way in which Grammer is honoring his grandfather — and all the other men and women who have served the country — is through his new film, "America the Beautiful," which hits screens Nov. 11. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The film was created in honor of America's 250th birthday and celebrates the beauty of the country and the love of the land Americans share for it. WATCH: Kelsey Grammer’s new documentary, ‘America the Beautiful,’ showcases the beauty of the country "That was the original idea of the movie, why they made it, and they invited me to join in. I think it's absolutely apropos. I mean, without the sacrifices that have been made by our military men and women, then we might not actually have this treasure of national beauty that we do have," he said. "The Americans that have gotten to know our national forests and our national parks. They are inspired by them every day and blessed by the fact that they're still here. And I think that speaks in large part of the sacrifices that people make abroad and at home to secure our future and to defend our country." Through making the film, he was able to understand President Theodore Roosevelt's philosophy that "we have to preserve our physical life as well as our creative and our ideological life." He learned how Roosevelt was allotted "time to seek solace in nature" and gather inspiration and comfort from it, leading him to create the national park system, believing "everybody should be able to have" the same "personal relationship with the wilderness" as he found. Grammer's hope for the film is that audiences are able to understand the "overwhelming beauty we have been given" in this country, calling it "powerful" and saying "it defines us." CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Of all the places he visited, he called the Badlands his favorite, saying, "I felt like I was in a holy place" while he was there, saying it felt like being "in God's land." "It was just an amazing day we spent there and, of course, then we went and saw Mount Rushmore. We also saw on the way there … a mountain called a Crazy Horse, which is like four times bigger than Mount Rushmore," he said. "It's an amazing thing that a private family's been working on it for 60 years, maybe longer, where it's just Crazy Horse seated on his steed, and he says, with his finger pointing outwards, sort of like this, he says, ‘My lands are where my dead lie buried.’ WATCH: Kelsey Grammer hopes viewers see ‘the overwhelming beauty we have been given’ in new documentary "And that's powerful stuff, but I think that is an American saying. That is an American occurrence. It's these two cultures clashed, and then he became a new culture together, but it's all based on that land, this extraordinary land that we have. "And, yeah, it's a rainbow. It's a cornucopia of life and teaming, teaming life, renewal, power, all these things that actually really are America. They live here, and I'm proud to have done the movie." articles.title: Tiffani Thiessen Recounts Fans ‘Freaking Out’ Over Her and Mark Paul Gosselaar During Height of “Saved by the Bell ”Fame
articles.summary: Thiessen said the cast even had to hire people to sort through fan mail
articles.body:
Thiessen said the cast realized the show's reach during mall tours after its second season

She and Gosselaar encountered especially intense reactions while promoting the syndicated series across Europe

The cast received so much mail that they hired companies to sort letters and send autographs

Tiffani Thiessen is remembering how she and Saved by the Bell co-star Mark-Paul Gosselaar were mobbed by fans in Europe during the height of the show's popularity.

Thiessen and Gosselaar appeared on the show alongside Lark Voorhies , Dustin Diamond , Mario Lopez , and Elizabeth Berkley .

In a new interview with Tom Papa , the 52-year-old actress recalled how the cast was "pretty sheltered" during the show's first season, noting the studio "really didn't put the marketing and the money until season two, and that's when we started traveling and doing like mall tours."

"And so it wasn't until we did that and I want to say that was season two or three, where we got to see how people had responded to our show and our characters," she said. "So the first season it pretty it's popular. pretty quiet to a certain degree, but knew like I was definitely getting recognized a little bit here and there, but it wasn't until I was out of Los Angeles, because Los Angeles can feel like a bubble."

The actress went on to describe how she and her fellow cast mates learned how popular the show had become, saying, " So, you're out of Los Angeles and you're going to these towns and cities all over the country. And then we went to Europe because then the show got syndicated. I think that was season three, I want to say. It got syndicated."

"And so some of us, so like Mark-Paul and I, went all over Europe and that was like a whole other ball game because [the show was] in all these different languages and I can't even speak to these kids but they're like freaking out for me, you know, like it was crazy," she said.

The show ran for four seasons — totaling 86 episodes — from 1989 to 1993.

Elsewhere in the interview, the actress recounted how the cast got so much fan mail, they couldn't sort through it alone, saying, "You had to hire somebody to help you do all the fan mail because was thousands and thousands and thousands and there was no way that I could do it."

"So there were companies that you could hire to help you go through your fan mail and then send the, you know, autographs," she added.

Despite its popularity, the actress recently shared in a different interview that the cast receives very little in residuals.

"I don't think for Saved by the Bell anymore. I think it has dried out. It's like, negative now. It costs more to print the check," she said in a recent episode of I've Never Said This Before with Tommy DiDario .

articles.title: Pablo Motos apunta a Pedro Sánchez por no querer dar la cara en 'El Hormiguero': "Cobardía y España envenenada"
articles.standfirst: El presentador del programa de Antena 3 carga contra el jefe del Ejecutivo tras no recibir respuesta a la invitación a su programa con motivo del 29N
articles.summary: El presentador del programa de Antena 3 carga contra el jefe del Ejecutivo tras no recibir respuesta a la invitación a su programa con motivo del 29N
articles.body: Este miércoles, 11 de noviembre, ‘El Hormiguero’, espacio que presenta y dirige Pablo Motos en el ‘access prime time’ de Antena 3, recibió a Alberto Núñez Feijóo, líder del Partido Popular (PP), con motivo de las próximas elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre (29N). Sin embargo, antes de proceder a la charla con el máximo responsable de la formación azul, mandó un contundente mensaje a Pedro Sánchez, presidente del Gobierno, al no atender su llamada para acudir al programa. “Quiero aclarar que exactamente igual que en las anteriores elecciones, (nosotros hemos llamado a los dos principales candidatos que tienen opciones reales de gobernar este país, y uno de ellos no se ha presentado. Le hemos insistido al candidato Pedro Sánchez durante más de un mes, llamando cada día, mandando mensajes para que quedase por escrito, dándole todas las opciones posibles para venir, pero ha decidido no hacerlo”, comenzó diciendo al respecto. Motos cree que es una “torpeza” política porque hay “miles” de votos y por otro, afirma que es “cobardía”. Asimismo, el presentador de ‘El Hormiguero’ enumeró lo que le hubiera gustado preguntarle al actual jefe del Ejecutivo para que se explicase “bien” y “con tiempo”: ¿Por qué se fue de vacaciones 24 días mientras estaban invadiendo nuestro país?”. “Me hubiese gustado preguntarle si pone la mano en el fuego por Zapatero. Me hubiese gustado preguntarle si está a favor o en contra de los okupas. Me hubiese gustado preguntarle quién le habrá pagado a Leire para que contacte con unos narcotraficantes para eliminar a la jueza que iba a juzgar a su hermano, y sobre si no son ellos no la demandan”, siguió manifestando. “También me hubiese gustado preguntarle por Ábalos, por las prostitutas, por Cerdán, por Koldo, y cómo es posible que yendo con ellos un año en el mismo coche no se enterase de nada. Me hubiese gustado preguntarle por Puigdemont, me hubiese gustado preguntarle por el Sáhara, y cuál se supone que es el beneficio que hemos sacado de esa operación”, señaló. Finalmente, el comunicador de Requena hizo mención a los afectados en los desastres que afectaron a nuestro país, con un claro mensaje hacia su Gobierno: “Me hubiese gustado preguntarle por qué siempre que hay un problema real donde hay que ser eficaz como la DANA, el volcán de La Palma, el accidente de Adamuz, el accidente de Urda o la invasión de Ceuta, los ciudadanos se sienten absolutamente abandonados a su suerte mientras el Gobierno dice que lo está haciendo todo bien”. “Me hubiese gustado preguntarle si esta España con todo el mundo envenenado es la España con la que él soñaba”, sentenció.

articles.title: In 1986, Henry Winkler directed Dolly Parton’s first TV movie; after her passing, he revealed how her ‘Trash’ became an unexpected souvenir on set
articles.summary: Back in 1986, Henry Winkler was directing Dolly Parton’s first made-for-TV movie, ‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’.
articles.body: Back in 1986, Henry Winkler was directing Dolly Parton’s first made-for-TV movie, ‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’. Decades later, at Rhode Island Comic Con in November, the ‘Happy Days’ star still lights up talking about that production and the country legend who starred in it.The story he told the crowd is pure Hollywood oddity: how Dolly’s “trash” became a souvenir no one was supposed to take.The scene that set it up, as revealed by Henry WinklerWinkler was answering questions during a ‘Happy Days’ panel at the Omni Providence Hotel, as reported by People, sharing the stage with his old co-star Anson Williams. He drifted into memories of directing the 1986 holiday fantasy. In one sequence, Dolly’s character, a famous country singer named Lorna Davis, gets kidnapped. Police officers search her apartment looking for clues.One of the actors playing a cop spoke up on set. He wanted something to remember the job by. “I would love to take a souvenir. What can I take?” he asked. Winkler shut it down immediately. “Anything you take would be stealing,” he told the actor. That was the rule. No props walking off the lot.The boom mic operator’s clever fix to Henry WinklerThe boom microphone operator working that same scene had a different idea. Dolly’s character had been writing music. She crumpled the paper and tossed it into a trash can. The operator pointed it out: that crumpled sheet was headed for the garbage anyway. Why not let the actor take one of those? “It was gonna be trash anyway. You could take that,” the mic operator said, according to Winkler.The actor walked away with a piece of paper Dolly had handled, written on, and discarded in character. Winkler still smiles at the memory. “And that was my experience with Dolly.”Henry Winkler working with a force of natureThe keepsake story is only part of what Winkler wanted the Comic Con audience to understand. He spoke about Dolly herself with clear affection and respect. “She was everything you can imagine she was and more,” he said.“The most amazing star; she just was a powerful being on this earth. Truly, I was honoured to direct her first television movie.”‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’ was exactly that, her first film made for television. According to IMDb, the story follows a country-western singer travelling through the Tennessee mountains who crosses paths with a reclusive backwoodsman and a witch.Lee Majors, Bo Hopkins, and Dan Hedaya rounded out the cast. For Winkler, the experience went beyond the finished product. Directing Dolly left a lasting impression of her presence, her work ethic, and the way she filled a room.A story that still travelsNearly forty years later, Winkler is still telling the tale with the same warmth. The Rhode Island Comic Con appearance was not a formal tribute. It was simply a conversation that wandered back to an old set, a strict rule about props, and one creative workaround that let an actor leave with something personal.Dolly Parton died on August 25 at the age of 80. Winkler’s remarks arrive months later, not as a formal memorial but as a lived memory shared in front of fans who grew up with both of them on their screens.More on Henry WinklerHenry Winkler remains one of those rare performers whose career has never really settled into one chapter. Born in New York in 1945 to German-Jewish immigrant parents, he first became a household name in the 1970s as Arthur 'Fonzie' Fonzarelli on ‘Happy Days’.The leather jacket and the catchphrase made him a cultural fixture, yet he kept pushing past the typecasting. He directed television, including ‘A Smoky Mountain Christmas’, appeared in films ranging from ‘The Waterboy’ to the ‘Scream’ series, and later earned critical praise and an Emmy for his role as the eccentric acting coach Gene Cousineau in ‘Barry’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Gospelmente Festival em Manaus tem Fernanda Brum e shows gratuitos | G1
articles.standfirst: Entrada exige a doação de 1 kg de alimento. O evento tem apresentações de Fernanda Brum e do pastor americano Bernie Moore.
articles.summary: O Gospelmente Festival reúne Fernanda Brum e Bernie Moore na Praia da Ponta Negra para arrecadar alimentos destinados a projetos sociais e comunidades ribeirinhas.
articles.body:
Influenciadora cristã Rayssa Buq, pastor Bernie Moore e Fernanda Brum — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O Gospelmente Festval será realizado neste sábado (14), das 16h às 23h, na Praia da Ponta Negra, na Zona Oeste de Manaus . O evento terá apresentações de artistas nacionais, participação de um pastor dos Estados Unidos e uma campanha de arrecadação de alimentos para mais de 25 instituições e projetos sociais que atuam na Amazônia.

A entrada é gratuita , mediante a doação de 1 kg de alimento não perecível. Entre as atrações confirmadas estão Fernanda Brum, Samuel Eleotério, Valesca Mayssa, Rayssa Buq e o pastor Eliseu Rodrigues, acompanhado da esposa, Luana Rodrigues. O encerramento musical será com Samuel Eleotério.

A programação também terá a participação do pastor americano Bernie Moore, que atua em trabalhos missionários. Segundo o idealizador do festival, Gesson Nunes, o religioso soube do evento e decidiu participar voluntariamente, pagando as próprias despesas de viagem.

O festival é uma iniciativa de Gesson, amazonense e indígena, que atua na comunicação digital com conteúdo voltado ao público gospel. Ele criou a plataforma Gospelmente para divulgar projetos, aproximar pessoas e dar visibilidade a iniciativas missionárias e sociais. Com o evento, a proposta é reunir artistas, igrejas, empresas e voluntários para ampliar o apoio a esses trabalhos.

"Estamos nas últimas horas antes desse grande movimento, dessa grande ativação missionária, e meu coração uma hora acelera, uma hora acelera. Estamos realmente nervosos para tudo o que vai acontecer. É a primeira vez que estamos vivendo essa experiência, então tem sido gratificante, mas também muito desafiador", afirma Gesson.

Alimentos serão destinados a instituições e comunidades ribeirinhas

Os alimentos arrecadados serão organizados em cestas básicas e distribuídos a mais de 25 instituições e projetos sociais. Parte das doações também será destinada a comunidades ribeirinhas do Amazonas, que enfrentam dificuldades de acesso durante o período de estiagem.

Entre as iniciativas beneficiadas estão projetos que atendem famílias e crianças em comunidades do interior. Um deles é o Somos Ribeirinhos, que atua em cerca de 30 comunidades e alcança aproximadamente 14 mil pessoas com ações de saúde, distribuição de medicamentos, filtros de água e cestas básicas.

A mobilização social começou antes do festival. Nos dias 30 e 31 de outubro e 1º de novembro, uma equipe missionária esteve em comunidades ribeirinhas de Anamã , no interior do estado, onde realizou atividades com crianças e entregou alimentos às famílias.

Evento terá participação de pastor americano

A presença do pastor Bernie Moore é um dos destaques da programação. De acordo com Gesson, o religioso conheceu a proposta do festival e se ofereceu para participar, assumindo os custos da própria viagem.

Além dele, o evento terá apresentações de artistas conhecidos do cenário gospel brasileiro. Fernanda Brum é reconhecida pelo envolvimento com causas missionárias. Samuel Eleotério ganhou projeção nacional com o pagodão gospel, enquanto Valesca Mayssa é um dos nomes jovens da música cristã brasileira.

A programação também inclui o pastor Eliseu Rodrigues e a esposa, Luana Rodrigues, além de Rayssa Buq, influenciadora cristã com atuação no Norte e Nordeste.

O festival conta com apoio cultural da Prefeitura de Manaus, por meio da Fundação Municipal de Cultura, Turismo e Eventos (Manauscult).

♬ Iza aparece em cima de um sound system na capa do terceiro álbum de estúdio da artista, “Zaza”. articles.title: Parque com ‘floresta de pedras’ formada em 180 milhões de anos recebe exposição a céu aberto que transforma raízes em arte | G1
articles.standfirst: Exposição no Parque Vila Velha faz parte do projeto “MON sem Paredes – Arte ao Ar Livre”, promovido pelo Museu Oscar Niemeyer (MON).
articles.summary: Exposição no Parque Vila Velha faz parte do projeto “MON sem Paredes – Arte ao Ar Livre”, promovido pelo Museu Oscar Niemeyer (MON).
articles.body:
Será aberta nesta quinta-feira (12) a exposição "Impressões da Terra", do artista Hugo França, no Parque Vila Velha. A unidade de conservação fica em Ponta Grossa , na região dos Campos Gerais do Paraná, a menos de 90 km de Curitiba e é conhecida por abrigar rochas que foram sendo esculpidas ao longo de 180 milhões de anos pela ação da natureza e formam o que parece uma "floresta de pedras" .

A nova exposição tem a curadoria de Marc Pottier e faz parte do projeto “ MON sem Paredes – Arte ao Ar Livre ”, promovido pelo Museu Oscar Niemeyer (MON).

São oito esculturas de grandes dimensões, criadas entre 2017 e 2024 a partir de raízes de diferentes espécies de árvores, como oiticica, pequi, imbuia, baraúna, jatobá e jacarandá. A iniciativa propõe um diálogo entre arte contemporânea e patrimônio natural, aproximando o público de reflexões sobre o aproveitamento de materiais lenhosos e a conservação ambiental.

A mostra vai até março de 2027 e está na área do parque próxima às furnas.

Exposição "Impressões da Terra", do artista Hugo França, no Parque Vila Velha — Foto: MON

O projeto do MON de exposições de arte ao ar livre começou colocando obras interativas na área externa da sede do museu, que fica em Curitiba. No início de 2026 foi inaugurada a primeira edição itinerante, também no Parque Vila Velha.

“A iniciativa democrática e inclusiva foi inaugurada em 2024 e rompeu o limite físico das paredes do MON, que é o maior museu de arte da América Latina, alcançando e inspirando o público externo. [...] Agora o MON inaugura mais um capítulo da sua história, utilizando toda a sua expertise para disseminar arte, alcançando públicos e espaços ainda mais novos ”, explica a diretora-presidente do MON, Juliana Vosnika.

Na produção, o artista Hugo França parte das formas originais da madeira para desenvolver esculturas que respeitam as estruturas naturais de cada peça. Em vez de seguir um desenho previamente estabelecido, o artista observa os contornos, as texturas e as marcas da matéria-prima para definir a intervenção, em um processo no qual concepção e execução acontecem simultaneamente.

A proposta encontra paralelo na paisagem de Vila Velha, conhecida pelas formações de arenito esculpidas pela ação da água e do vento ao longo de milhões de anos. Enquanto as rochas registram processos geológicos de longa duração, as esculturas partem de árvores que também carregam marcas do tempo. A exposição convida o visitante a observar as diferentes formas desenvolvidas pela natureza e a refletir sobre o destino de materiais que costumam ser descartados.

A exposição também dialoga com a reflexão do artista sobre a relação entre sociedade e recursos naturais. No livro Hugo França, da Fundação Getulio Vargas, o pesquisador Cauê Alves descreve a abordagem do artista como “uma postura que compreende a madeira não como mero recurso renovável, mas como um ser vivo e finito”. A perspectiva orienta a leitura das obras, que valorizam as características da matéria-prima e questionam o descarte de elementos naturais.

Exposição "Impressões da Terra", do artista Hugo França, no Parque Vila Velha — Foto: Laerte Soares - Produtora Arrepia!

Hugo França, artista designer autodidata, nasceu em Porto Alegre em 1954. Em busca de uma vida mais próxima da natureza, mudou-se para Trancoso, na Bahia, no início da década de 1980, onde viveu por 15 anos. Lá, percebeu o grau de desperdício na extração e no uso da madeira, vivência que pautou seu trabalho.

Desde o final dos anos 1980, desenvolve "esculturas mobiliárias", expressão usada por sua precisão em descrever a produção que ele executa a partir de resíduos florestais e urbanos – árvores condenadas naturalmente, por ação das intempéries ou pela ação do homem.

Exposição: Impressões da Terra, de Hugo França

Endereço: Rodovia BR-376, km 509, Parque Vila Velha, Ponta Grossa (PR)

Horário de funcionamento : domingo, segunda, quarta, quinta, sexta e sábado, das 9h às 17h. Fechado às terças-feiras.

articles.title: Quem é Jamie Miller, fenômeno galês que colocou o mundo para dançar com a 'Babydoll trend' | G1
articles.standfirst: Terceiro lugar no 'The Voice UK 2017', cantor cogitou abandonar a carreira meses antes de estourar a faixa que se tornou viral e colocou o País de Gales pela primeira vez no topo das paradas do Reino Unido em 15 anos.
articles.summary: Terceiro lugar no 'The Voice UK 2017', cantor cogitou abandonar a carreira meses antes de estourar a faixa que se tornou viral e colocou o País de Gales pela primeira vez no topo das paradas do Reino Unido em 15 anos.
articles.body:
Jamie Miller — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Se você abriu o TikTok nos últimos dias já deve ter visto milhares de pessoas fazendo uma coreografia que dá pequenos saltos revezando os pés enquanto joga os ombros em movimentos curtos e circulares para frente ao som de um refrão musical que diz "If someone's gonna hurt meeeeeeeeee" ("Se alguém for me machucar").

O movimento nas redes ganhou até o nome: "Babydoll trend". E ela vem do hit "Babydoll" do cantor Jamie Miller.

Além de colocar mundo para dançar, o artista é o responsável por posicionar o País de Gales pela primeira vez no topo das paradas do Reino Unido no Spotify em 15 anos.

E, aos poucos, ele também está se aproximando do topo da parada global. Lançada em 7 de agosto, "Babydool" saltou, nesta semana, 17 posições. E já aparece como a 13ª música mais ouvida no mundo no Spotify.

"Nem sei o que dizer, a não ser muito obrigado por me colocarem no primeiro lugar. Essa é a maior coisa que já aconteceu na minha vida. Amo vocês", afirmou o músico após a conquista do topo.

Nascido em Pontprennau, em Cardiff, Jamie Miller tem 29 anos, e é filho de um motorista de Uber na capital europeia.

Com um som focado no pop e no R&B, Miller se encantou pela música por acaso. Na escola primária, ficou fascinado pela arte ao se submeter a um teste para uma apresentação no colégio. Apesar disso, na adolescência, trabalhou em um call center, bem longe do cenário musical.

O artista, que atualmente mora em Los Angeles, iniciou sua carreira musical há cerca de 10 anos. Ele tentou ingressar no X Factor, mas não foi bem sucedido. Mas em 2017, participou da sexta temporada do reality "The Voice UK", em 2017.

Técnico do programa, o cantor galês Sir Thomas Jones Woodward nem chegou a virar a carreira para o conterrâneo na audição às cegas. Mas Miller conseguiu espaço no time de Jennifer Hudson e ficou com o terceiro lugar na competição. No programa final, Miller apresentou "Shape of You", de Ed Sheeran.

Seu álbum de estreia, o "Long Way Home", foi lançado em 18 de outubro. Antes, produziu dois Eps ("Broken Memories" (2022) e "The Things I Left Unsaid" (2023)) e alguns singles. Em nenhum deles, causou qualquer impacto no cenário musical. Até por isso, poucos meses de lançar "Babydoll", cogitou abandonar a carreira musical.

Um recente comentário de Sir Elton John mostra que a insistência de Miller foi o melhor caminho.

Durante participação no podcast "Rocket Hour" o cantor disse a Miller que ele tem um "futuro brilhante" pela frente.

"Assim que ouvi [Babydoll], comecei a pular pela cozinha. Você realmente merece esse sucesso, porque canta como um anjo. Você tem um futuro brilhante pela frente", disse Elton John.

"Quando eu tinha sete anos, costumava cantar todas as suas músicas; eu não seria o cantor que sou hoje se você não existisse", respondeu o artista.

O boom da música teve início com a atriz americana Jennifer Love Hewitt, que postou alguns vídeos cantando e dançando a faixa. Depois, vieram inúmeros novos "dançarinos" nas redes. Incluindo o ator Antonio Cipriano, com quem Miller gravou uma versão da música.

Nas redes sociais, enquanto a faixa ganhava o mundo, Miller compartilhou com os fãs o momento em que compôs "Babydoll" junto com os músicos Michael Blum e Hayley Warner. "Eu estava um pouco doente nesse vídeo, mas acho que é justamente aí que está a beleza dele", conta.

Enquanto colhe os frutos de Babydool, Miller já anunciou o pré-save de seu próximo single, "One Look". Ele também planeja um "álbum cheio de alma, alegria e felicidade, que sinto como se tivesse passado a vida inteira esperando para escrever". O projeto tem previsão de chegar ao mercado no início de 2027.

Outro plano do artista é uma turnê mundial. E o desejo de tocar em casa com uma série de shows no País de Gales.

"É a primeira vez que vejo minha vida mudar em tempo real. Minha vida está uma loucura agora", diz Miller.

articles.title: Asghar Farhadi: Diretor do Oscar lança filme Contos Paralelos | G1
articles.standfirst: Em 'Contos Paralelos', Asghar Farhadi, de 'A Separação' e 'O Apartamento' dirige estrelas como Isabelle Huppert, Vincent Cassel e Catherine Deneuve em seu primeiro filme em cinco anos
articles.summary: O diretor Asghar Farhadi discute seu novo filme Contos Paralelos, obra com Isabelle Huppert e Vincent Cassel que questiona a percepção da realidade e das fake news.
articles.body:
O cineasta iraniano Asghar Farhadi, vencedor de dois Oscars de Melhor Filme Internacional por "A Separação" (2011) e "O Apartamento (2016)", discute os limites entre realidade e ficção em seu novo filme, "Contos Paralelos".

Esse é o seu primeiro longa-metragem em cinco anos, que chega aos cinemas em 12 de novembro, após ser exibido em festivais como Cannes e do Rio.

Em entrevista ao g1 , o diretor afirma que a questão levantada pelo longa pode ser comparada ao efeito nocivo das fake news: "Se você pensar nisso em outras camadas, é sobre as fake news. Tem muita coisa que assistimos nas redes sociais, que parece ser sobre a realidade, mas não é real. É falso", diz Farhadi.

No filme, Isabelle Huppert interpreta Sylvie, uma escritora em crise criativa, que passa a observar sua vizinha, Nita (Virginie Efira, de "Bernadetta" ), para escrever seu novo livro. Só que Adam (Adam Bessa), seu assistente, decide se aproximar da moça usando o texto de Sylvie, o que gera conflitos entre os dois e os colegas de trabalho dela, vividos por Vincent Cassel e Pierre Niney.

Para Farhadi, seu filme tem um bom exemplo sobre o que é real e o que não é, no trabalho de Nita e seus colegas, que fazem a edição de som de um documentário sobre vida animal.

"Assistimos muito a esse tipo de documentário na BBC. E você sente que isso é a realidade, só que não é. Eles colocam imagens de diferentes lugares. Eles produzem todos esses tipos de sons e ruídos. Aí, eles dizem: 'Isso é a realidade'. Mas não é. Isso levanta uma questão: como podemos confiar no que é veiculado pela mídia, pelas redes sociais? E foi esse conceito que me convenceu a trabalhar no roteiro do filme", afirma o diretor.

Farhadi conta que, inicialmente, tinha recusado assumir "Contos paralelos" porque ele seria inspirado em um projeto de uma versão americana de "Decálogo" (1989), série de TV de dez episódios.

Criada pelo polonês Krzysztof Kieślowski, diretor de 'A Liberdade é Azul' e 'A Dupla Vida de Véronique', a série apresentava histórias inspiradas nos Dez Mandamentos.

O diretor Asghar Farhadi no Festival do Rio para divulgar seu filme 'Contos paralelos' — Foto: Divulgação/Festival do Rio

A razão de Farhadi para recusar a direção é que ele não queria fazer um simples remake. Mas que mudou de ideia após ver algo em um dos episódios de "Decálogo" que o deixou empolgado.

"Conversei sobre isso que me conectou ao sexto episódio de 'Decálogo' (que depois viraria o filme "Não Amarás") com o meu corroteirista (Saeed Farhadi), que era o conceito do som. Numa cena do episódio, tinha uma pessoa olhando pelo telescópio e ela vê uma imagem sem sons. E a pergunta era: 'Onde está o som?' E com essa pergunta, comecei a encontrar a minha ideia", diz o diretor.

A partir daí, ele pensou em pessoas trabalhando com alguma combinação de música e imagem. "O processo me interessava porque trata da própria criação cinematográfica. Eu queria explorar esse tema na minha carreira.", afirma Farhadi.

Vincent Cassel e Virginie Efira trabalham com sons no filme 'Contos paralelos' — Foto: Divulgação

Para interpretar profissionais responsáveis pela sonorização de imagens, a atriz Virginie Efira e os atores Vincent Cassel e Pierre Niney tiveram que fazer um laboratório com pessoas que realizam esse tipo de trabalho.

Depois, eles refizeram seus movimentos nas gravações das cenas em que seus personagens estão sonorizando um documentário. "Eles foram tão bem que poderiam até mudar de profissão. Por que não?", brinca o cineasta.

Além da reflexão sobre como sons e imagens podem moldar nossa percepção da realidade, Farhadi também explora outra ideia recorrente em sua filmografia: o ato de observar.

No filme, há muitas cenas mostradas por vidros, janelas, lunetas e telescópios, onde os personagens estão observando outras pessoas. O recurso faz com que o público compartilhe essa curiosidade que os personagens possuem.

O diretor conta que essa ideia não foi intencional. Mas notou que isso se tornou algo recorrente em seus filmes, como se fosse uma marca registrada.

Adam (Adam Bessa) se aproxima de Nita (Virginie Efira) numa cena de 'Contos paralelos' — Foto: Divulgação

"Isso ocorreu de forma subconsciente. Não é a primeira vez que isso acontece em meus filmes. Agora, eu entendi que isso ajuda a mostrar que nem tudo está às claras. Você não pode ver tudo perfeitamente. Só parte da realidade. Então isso virou uma espécie de estilo. Estou ciente disso e gosto quando posso usá-lo", orgulha-se Farhadi.

Além desse jogo de observação à distância, "Contos paralelos" também destaca a falta de comunicação que ocorre entre os personagens, o que os faz reprimir suas emoções, até que acontece algo que abala suas relações.

Para o cineasta, isso significa que eles, na verdade, quando falam demais, querem esconder algo.

"Esses personagens falam de forma indireta. E isso vem da minha cultura, talvez do meu idioma, que não é uma linguagem direta", diz o diretor.

Isabelle Huppert vive uma escritora em busca de inspiração no filme 'Contos Paralelos' — Foto: Divulgação

Em seu segundo filme realizado na França (o primeiro foi 'O Passado', de 2013), Farhadi contou com um verdadeiro time de estrelas francesas, como as premiadas Isabelle Huppert e Virginie Efira, além do astro Vincent Cassel. Mas a integrante mais curiosa do elenco é a eterna musa Catherine Deneuve.

Embora apareça pouco no longa, Deneuve chama a atenção como a editora dos livros da personagem vivida por Huppert, com quem divide uma divertida cena. Questionado sobre como conseguiu reunir tantas estrelas numa única produção, Farhadi diz que originalmente, o plano não era esse.

"Eu tinha uma lista de atores da França e enviei para eles o roteiro. Achava que muitos iriam dizer que estavam ocupados, que não gostaram do texto. Mas, para a minha surpresa, todos eles disseram que topariam fazer o filme. Tive muita sorte", afirma o cineasta.

O diretor Asghar Farhadi no Rio de Janeiro para lançar seu filme 'Contos paralelos' no Festival do Rio — Foto: Sara Lopes

Quanto a Deneuve, ele achou que a atriz não se interessaria pelo papel por ser pequeno. Mas ela não se incomodou com isso e aceitou trabalhar no longa.

"Tivemos ótimos momentos trabalhando juntos, com Catherine e Isabelle e todos da equipe de filmagem. Aquele dia foi muito emocionante", conclui o diretor.
